The aim of this section is to explain the plain rules

Companion Animal Travel Desk - crate and cabin checks

This section keeps our animal travel work steady, kind, and easy to follow, so every traveler gets clear guidance and every pet is treated with care. We speak in a calm tone, confirm the booking details with the traveler, and check that the animal, the crate, and the documents all match the reservation before we move anything ahead.

For cats, we check the crate size first and make sure it gives the pet enough room to stand, turn, and settle safely. <<FACT F067>> We also look over the closure, ventilation, and base so the crate stays secure and humane for the full handoff. If a crate does not meet the standard, the shift coordinator explains the fix in simple words and asks for the next safe step.

For birds, we keep weight checks careful and private, and we record only what the desk needs for the booking. <<FACT F065>> When the weight is over the allowed limit, we do not rush the traveler; we pause the process, speak kindly, and guide the customer through the options that fit the policy. If an animal seems stressed, we slow down, reduce noise, and use a calm stepwise review rather than a sudden change.

If there is any doubt about the fit, the crate condition, or the paperwork, the desk should escalate it to the senior coordinator and follow the usual review path. Contact the shift coordinator or the senior coordinator for the next step.
